newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Labor Minister rejects pay hike pressures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Labor Minister rejects pay hike pressures.

text.p: Labor Minister Javier Bonilla rejected pressure from union movements to ask the government to consider an emergency increase in salaries.
A salary rise would be a break from Mexico's tripartite "pacto" or "alliance" among the government, business sectors and labor factions.
Bonilla told reporters Thursday night, "The alliance continues to work well. We have to keep working hard and there is no change foreseen to the terms of the accord that was signed last October."
The alliance is a mechanism worked out by the three parties each year setting wage increases and price hikes for controlled products -- aiming to keep a lid on inflation.
Union leaders have called for an increase in salaries because the original alliance had intended to give workers a hike this year above inflation levels.

"There will have to be a forced adjustment in the level of minimum wage because the alliance had always contemplated that salaries would go up two percentage points higher than inflation," labor leader Enrique Aguilar Borrego told reporters Thursday.

Borrego, vice-chairman of the Labor Congress, is one of the top labor sector spokesmen pushing for a revision. His argument is that inflation will end the year higher than government forecasts, hence the need for higher salaries.
Mexico's nonegenarian union boss Fidel Velazquez, head of the Mexican Workers Confederation, has also planted the idea of an adjustment in the terms of the original pact.
